prompt: Estimate $\int_0^4 x^2 \, dx$ using a left Riemann sum with $4$ equal subintervals.
hint: Four subintervals on $[0, 4]$ means each has width $\Delta x = 1$. A LEFT sum uses the left endpoint of each: $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$.

hints.text: Four subintervals on $[0, 4]$ means each has width $\Delta x = 1$. A LEFT sum uses the left endpoint of each: $x = 0, 1, 2, 3$.
Add the heights $f(0) + f(1) + f(2) + f(3)$ and multiply by the width $1$.

explanation: Left sum $= 1 \cdot (0 + 1 + 4 + 9) = 14$. Since $x^2$ is increasing, this underestimates the true area, which is $\frac{64}{3} \approx 21.3$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Draw the rectangles
steps: On $[0, 1]$ the rectangle has height $f(0) = 0$ — it is flat, contributing nothing.
On $[1, 2]$, height $1$; on $[2, 3]$, height $4$; on $[3, 4]$, height $9$.
Each rectangle sits below the rising curve, so the total $14$ is an underestimate.
